   23|       |/// Planner for S3 adapter actions.
   24|       |///
   25|       |/// For S3 mutating operations + S3Object, generates an execution plan with:
   26|       |///
   27|       |/// - **prepare_checks**: `S3ObjectExists` (if the operation expects the object to exist)
   28|       |/// - **verify_checks**: `S3VersionIdMatches` placeholder (to be filled after execute)
   29|       |/// - **compensation_plan**: A placeholder `s3.versioning_rollback_v1` step with
   30|       |///   `before_version_id` and `after_version_id` args to be filled at execution time.
   31|       |///
   32|       |/// Read-only operations (`S3GetObject`) produce no compensation plan.
   33|       |pub struct PlannableS3Adapter;
   34|       |
   35|       |#[async_trait]
   36|       |impl PlannableAdapter for PlannableS3Adapter {
   37|       |    async fn generate_plan(
   38|       |        &self,
   39|       |        action_type: &ActionType,
   40|       |        target: &RollbackTarget,
   41|      5|    ) -> Result<Option<ExecutionPlan>, AdapterError> {
   42|       |        match (action_type, target) {
   43|       |            (
   44|       |                ActionType::S3PutObject | ActionType::S3DeleteObject | ActionType::S3CopyObject,
   45|       |                RollbackTarget::S3Object { bucket, key, .. },
   46|       |            ) => {
   47|       |                let mut prepare_checks = Vec::new();
   48|       |                let mut verify_checks = Vec::new();
   49|       |                let mut compensation_plan = Vec::new();
   50|       |
   51|       |                // Prepare: validate object exists for Delete/Copy (not Put, which may create)
   52|       |                if matches!(
   53|      5|                    action_type,
   54|       |                    ActionType::S3DeleteObject | ActionType::S3CopyObject
   55|       |                ) {
   56|       |                    prepare_checks.push(ferrum_proto::CheckSpec {
   57|       |                        check_type: ferrum_proto::CheckType::S3ObjectExists,
   58|       |                        config: json_map_from_serde_map(
   59|       |                            serde_json::json!({
   60|       |                                "bucket": bucket.clone(),
   61|       |                                "key": key.clone()
   62|       |                            })
   63|       |                            .as_object()
   64|       |                            .unwrap()
   65|       |                            .clone(),
   66|       |                        ),
   67|       |                    });
   68|       |                }
   69|       |
   70|       |                // Verify: placeholder version check (to be filled after execute)
   71|       |                verify_checks.push(ferrum_proto::CheckSpec {
   72|       |                    check_type: ferrum_proto::CheckType::S3VersionIdMatches,
   73|       |                    config: json_map_from_serde_map(
   74|       |                        serde_json::json!({
   75|       |                            "bucket": bucket.clone(),
   76|       |                            "key": key.clone(),
   77|       |                            "expected_version_id": "TBD"
   78|       |                        })
   79|       |                        .as_object()
   80|       |                        .unwrap()
   81|       |                        .clone(),
   82|       |                    ),
   83|       |                });
   84|       |
   85|       |                // Compensation: placeholder versioning rollback step
   86|       |                compensation_plan.push(CompensationStep {
   87|       |                    order: 1,
   88|       |                    adapter_key: "s3".to_string(),
   89|       |                    operation: "s3.versioning_rollback_v1".to_string(),
   90|       |                    args: json_map_from_serde_map(
   91|       |                        serde_json::json!({
   92|       |                            "bucket": bucket.clone(),
   93|       |                            "key": key.clone(),
   94|       |                            "before_version_id": "TBD",
   95|       |                            "after_version_id": "TBD"
   96|       |                        })
   97|       |                        .as_object()
   98|       |                        .unwrap()
   99|       |                        .clone(),
  100|       |                    ),
  101|       |                    idempotency_key: next_idempotency_key(),
  102|       |                });
  103|       |
  104|       |                Ok(Some(ExecutionPlan {
  105|       |                    prepare_checks,
  106|       |                    verify_checks,
  107|       |                    compensation_plan,
  108|       |                    auto_commit: false,
  109|       |                    plan_description: format!("s3 {:?} plan for {}/{}", action_type, bucket, key),
  110|       |                }))
  111|       |            }
  112|       |            (ActionType::S3GetObject, RollbackTarget::S3Object { bucket, key, .. }) => {
  113|       |                // Read-only: no compensation, minimal checks
  114|       |                Ok(Some(ExecutionPlan {
  115|       |                    prepare_checks: Vec::new(),
  116|       |                    verify_checks: vec![ferrum_proto::CheckSpec {
  117|       |                        check_type: ferrum_proto::CheckType::S3ObjectExists,
  118|       |                        config: json_map_from_serde_map(
  119|       |                            serde_json::json!({
  120|       |                                "bucket": bucket.clone(),
  121|       |                                "key": key.clone()
  122|       |                            })
  123|       |                            .as_object()
  124|       |                            .unwrap()
  125|       |                            .clone(),
  126|       |                        ),
  127|       |                    }],
  128|       |                    compensation_plan: Vec::new(),
  129|       |                    auto_commit: true,
  130|       |                    plan_description: format!("s3 S3GetObject plan for {}/{}", bucket, key),
  131|       |                }))
  132|       |            }
  133|       |            _ => Ok(None), // Not plannable by this adapter
  134|       |        }
  135|      5|    }
  136|       |}

    1|       |//! S3 Object Lock WORM upload support.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! This module provides a small, bounded helper for uploading audit bundles to an
    4|       |//! S3-compatible object store with Object Lock. It is **not** a general-purpose S3
    5|       |//! admin tool: it does not create buckets, enable Object Lock, manage IAM, or
    6|       |//! perform deletes/retention bypasses.
    7|       |//!
    8|       |//! Live SDK calls are gated by the `s3-client` feature. Without it, the module
    9|       |//! falls back to shape validation and returns an explicit error if a live upload is
   10|       |//! requested. This keeps unit tests safe without credentials.
   11|       |
   12|       |use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
   13|       |use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
   14|       |use std::str::FromStr;
   15|       |use thiserror::Error;
   16|       |
   17|       |/// Supported S3 Object Lock modes.
   18|       |#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   19|       |#[serde(rename_all = "PascalCase")]
   20|       |pub enum ObjectLockMode {
   21|       |    /// Governance mode allows privileged users to alter retention.
   22|       |    Governance,
   23|       |    /// Compliance mode is stricter and cannot be bypassed by any user.
   24|       |    Compliance,
   25|       |}
   26|       |
   27|       |impl ObjectLockMode {
   28|      0|    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {
   29|      0|        match self {
   30|      0|            ObjectLockMode::Governance => "GOVERNANCE",
   31|      0|            ObjectLockMode::Compliance => "COMPLIANCE",
   32|       |        }
   33|      0|    }
   34|       |}
   35|       |

   37|       |    type Err = String;
   38|       |
   39|      3|    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
   40|      3|        match s.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
   41|      3|            "governance" => Ok(ObjectLockMode::Governance),
                                          ^1
   42|      2|            "compliance" => Ok(ObjectLockMode::Compliance),
                                          ^1
   43|      1|            _ => Err(format!(
   44|      1|                "invalid object_lock_mode '{}': expected 'governance' or 'compliance'",
   45|      1|                s
   46|      1|            )),
   47|       |        }
   48|      3|    }

  364|       |    async fn client(&self) -> Result<aws_sdk_s3::Client, WormUploadError> {
  365|       |        {
  366|       |            let lock = self.client.lock().unwrap();
  367|       |            if let Some(client) = lock.clone() {
  368|       |                return Ok(client);
  369|       |            }
  370|       |        }
  371|       |        let mut aws_cfg = aws_config::from_env()
  372|       |            .region(aws_sdk_s3::config::Region::new(self.config.region.clone()));
  373|       |        if let Some(ref endpoint) = self.config.endpoint_url {
  374|       |            aws_cfg = aws_cfg.endpoint_url(endpoint.clone());
  375|       |        }
  376|       |        if let (Some(key), Some(secret)) =
  377|       |            (&self.config.access_key_id, &self.config.secret_access_key)
  378|       |        {
  379|       |            let creds = aws_credential_types::Credentials::new(
  380|       |                key.clone(),
  381|       |                secret.clone(),
  382|       |                None,
  383|       |                None,
  384|       |                "ferrum-adapter-s3-worm",
  385|       |            );
  386|       |            aws_cfg = aws_cfg.credentials_provider(creds);
  387|       |        }
  388|       |        let shared_cfg = aws_cfg.load().await;
  389|       |        let mut s3_builder = aws_sdk_s3::config::Builder::from(&shared_cfg);
  390|       |        if self.config.endpoint_url.is_some() {
  391|       |            s3_builder = s3_builder.force_path_style(true);
  392|       |        }
  393|       |        let client = aws_sdk_s3::Client::from_conf(s3_builder.build());
  394|       |        let mut lock = self.client.lock().unwrap();
  395|       |        *lock = Some(client.clone());
  396|       |        Ok(client)
  397|       |    }

 1966|       |    #[tokio::test]
 1967|      1|    async fn test_verify_returns_verified_false_on_query_error_not_config_error() {
 1968|       |        // G-E1 fail-closed: query errors (DB locked, table not found, IO errors) during
 1969|       |        // a SqlRowCountRange check return verified=false.
 1970|       |        // NOTE: This is NOT a true DB-lock contention test. SQLite's Connection::open()
 1971|       |        // succeeds even when the DB is locked; the lock only manifests on query execution.
 1972|       |        // A genuine lock-contention test would require holding a write lock across another
 1973|       |        // connection with busy_timeout=5000ms, which is impractical for a fast unit test.
 1974|       |        // This test documents the actual fail-closed behavior for query errors.
 1975|       |
 1976|      1|        let temp_dir = tempdir().unwrap();
 1977|      1|        let db_path = temp_dir.path().join("test.db");
 1978|      1|        let db_path_str = db_path.display().to_string();
 1979|       |
 1980|      1|        let conn = Connection::open(&db_path).unwrap();
 1981|      1|        conn.execute_batch("CREATE TABLE items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)")
 1982|      1|            .unwrap();
 1983|      1|        drop(conn);
 1984|       |
 1985|      1|        let adapter = SqliteAdapter::new_unbounded("sqlite");
 1986|       |
 1987|       |        // verify_check that queries a nonexistent table triggers query error -> verified=false
 1988|      1|        let mut contract = create_test_contract(&db_path_str);
 1989|      1|        contract.verify_checks = vec![CheckSpec {
 1990|      1|            check_type: CheckType::SqlRowCountRange,
 1991|      1|            config: json_map_from_serde_map(
 1992|      1|                serde_json::json!({

   26|       |/// Planner for SQLite adapter actions.
   27|       |///
   28|       |/// For SqlMutation + SqliteTxn, generates an execution plan with:
   29|       |///
   30|       |/// - **prepare_checks**: SqlRowCountRange check on the target table (if table name known)
   31|       |/// - **verify_checks**: SqlRowCountRange to verify expected row count after mutation
   32|       |/// - **compensation_plan**: Rollback step with SQL reversed from the mutation
   33|       |///
   34|       |/// Note: The actual compensation SQL must be provided by the caller since the planner
   35|       |/// does not know the specific SQL statement at plan generation time. The test
   36|       |/// should populate the compensation_plan with the appropriate DELETE/INSERT statement
   37|       |/// before calling compensate.
   38|       |pub struct PlannableSqliteAdapter;
   39|       |
   40|       |#[async_trait]
   41|       |impl PlannableAdapter for PlannableSqliteAdapter {
   42|       |    async fn generate_plan(
   43|       |        &self,
   44|       |        action_type: &ActionType,
   45|       |        target: &RollbackTarget,
   46|      4|    ) -> Result<Option<ExecutionPlan>, AdapterError> {
   47|       |        match (action_type, target) {
   48|       |            // SqlMutation: DML operations (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE)
   49|       |            // The compensation_plan SQL must be provided by the caller since we don't
   50|       |            // know the specific SQL at plan time.
   51|       |            (ActionType::SqlMutation, RollbackTarget::SqliteTxn { db_path, tx_id: _ }) => {
   52|       |                // Table name extraction from db_path always returned None (dead code),
   53|       |                // so verify_checks remains empty. Caller should populate verify_checks
   54|       |                // with SqlRowCountRange checks if needed.
   55|       |
   56|       |                Ok(Some(ExecutionPlan {

crates/ferrum-audit-bundle/src/lib.rs:
    1|       |//! Portable, tamper-evident audit bundle format.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! This crate exposes the canonical bundle builder and verifier used by both
    4|       |//! `ferrumctl audit export/verify` and the gateway's optional WORM sink. The
    5|       |//! format is intentionally simple and self-contained:
    6|       |//!
    7|       |//! - `audit.jsonl` — one JSON Lines record per audit log entry, in chronological
    8|       |//!   order, preserving the original `content_hash` and `previous_hash` fields.
    9|       |//! - `manifest.json` — metadata including bundle version, export timestamp, first
   10|       |//!   and last content hash, entry count, and a Merkle root over the chain of
   11|       |//!   content hashes.
   12|       |//!
   13|       |//! The bundle is **not** encrypted by default; operators may encrypt at rest via
   14|       |//! filesystem or sink-level encryption.
   15|       |//!
   16|       |//! Verification re-computes the SHA-256 content hash for each entry, checks the
   17|       |//! hash chain continuity, and verifies the Merkle root. It does not make any
   18|       |//! compliance, WORM-certified, or tamper-proof claims.
   19|       |
   20|       |use chrono::Utc;
   21|       |use ferrum_proto::AuditLogEntry;
   22|       |use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
   23|       |use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
   24|       |use std::collections::HashSet;
   25|       |use std::fs;
   26|       |use std::path::Path;
   27|       |
   28|       |pub const AUDIT_JSONL: &str = "audit.jsonl";
   29|       |pub const MANIFEST_JSON: &str = "manifest.json";
   30|       |
   31|       |/// Errors that can occur while building, exporting, or verifying a bundle.
   32|       |#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
   33|       |pub enum AuditBundleError {
   34|       |    #[error("serialization error: {0}")]
   35|       |    Serialize(#[from] serde_json::Error),
   36|       |    #[error("I/O error: {0}")]
   37|       |    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),
   38|       |    #[error("invalid bundle: {0}")]
   39|       |    Invalid(String),
   40|       |}
   41|       |

   43|       |#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
   44|       |pub struct AuditBundleManifest {
   45|       |    pub version: u32,
   46|       |    pub exported_at: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>,
   47|       |    pub first_hash: String,

   66|       |/// Compute the deterministic SHA-256 content hash for an audit log entry.
   67|       |///
   68|       |/// Mirrors the server-side logic in `crates/ferrum-store/src/sqlite/audit_log.rs`
   69|       |/// and `crates/ferrum-store/src/postgres/audit_log.rs`. The hash covers the
   70|       |/// canonical fields and excludes `id`, `content_hash`, and `previous_hash` to
   71|       |/// avoid circularity.
   72|     42|pub fn compute_content_hash(entry: &AuditLogEntry) -> String {
   73|     42|    let canonical = serde_json::json!({
   74|     42|        "actor_id": entry.actor_id,
   75|     42|        "action": entry.action.to_string(),
   76|     42|        "resource_type": entry.resource_type.to_string(),
   77|     42|        "resource_id": entry.resource_id,
   78|     42|        "result": entry.result,
   79|     42|        "metadata": entry.metadata,
   80|     42|        "created_at": entry.created_at.to_rfc3339(),
   81|       |    });
   82|     42|    let bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&canonical).expect("canonical serialization");
   83|     42|    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
   84|     42|    hasher.update(&bytes);
   85|     42|    hex::encode(hasher.finalize())
   86|     42|}

   88|       |/// Compute a deterministic Merkle root over a list of hex-encoded content hashes.
   89|       |///
   90|       |/// Mirrors the server-side logic in `crates/ferrum-store/src/merkle.rs`. An empty
   91|       |/// hash list returns an empty root.
   92|     21|pub fn compute_merkle_root(hashes: &[String]) -> String {
   93|     21|    if hashes.is_empty() {
   94|      0|        return String::new();
   95|     21|    }
   96|       |
   97|     21|    let mut level: Vec<Vec<u8>> = hashes
   98|     21|        .iter()
   99|     33|        .map(|h| {
                       ^21
  100|     33|            let bytes = hex::decode(h).expect("valid hex content_hash");
  101|     33|            let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
  102|     33|            hasher.update([0x00]);
  103|     33|            hasher.update(&bytes);
  104|     33|            hasher.finalize().to_vec()
  105|     33|        })
  106|     21|        .collect();
  107|       |
  108|     33|    while level.len() > 1 {
  109|     12|        let mut next_level = Vec::new();
  110|     12|        let mut i = 0;
  111|     24|        while i < level.len() {
  112|     12|            let left = &level[i];
  113|     12|            let right = if i + 1 < level.len() {
  114|     12|                &level[i + 1]
  115|       |            } else {
  116|      0|                left
  117|       |            };
  118|     12|            let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
  119|     12|            hasher.update([0x01]);
  120|     12|            hasher.update(left);
  121|     12|            hasher.update(right);
  122|     12|            next_level.push(hasher.finalize().to_vec());
  123|     12|            i += 2;
  124|       |        }
  125|     12|        level = next_level;
  126|       |    }
  127|       |
  128|     21|    hex::encode(&level[0])
  129|     21|}

  244|       |    /// Redact common secret patterns from a string.
  245|       |    ///
  246|       |    /// Targets: bearer/authorization tokens, API keys, GitHub tokens, AWS
  247|       |    /// access-key-like values, PEM private key markers.  Preserves UUIDs and
  248|       |    /// correlation IDs (high-confidence, low false-positive design).
  249|  1.60k|    fn redact_secrets(input: &str) -> String {
  250|       |        use regex::Regex;
  251|       |        use std::sync::LazyLock;
  252|       |
  253|      6|        static PATTERNS: LazyLock<Vec<Regex>> = LazyLock::new(|| {
  254|      6|            vec![
  255|       |                // PEM private key blocks (match first to avoid partial matches)
  256|      6|                Regex::new(r"(?i)-----BEGIN\s+(?:ENCRYPTED\s+|RSA\s+|EC\s+|OPENSSH\s+|DSA\s+)?PRIVATE\s+KEY-----[A-Za-z0-9\s+/=]*?-----END\s+(?:ENCRYPTED\s+|RSA\s+|EC\s+|OPENSSH\s+|DSA\s+)?PRIVATE\s+KEY-----")
  257|      6|                    .expect("valid static PEM regex"),
  258|       |                // GitHub tokens
  259|      6|                Regex::new(r"\bgh[opusr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}\b")
  260|      6|                    .expect("valid static GitHub token regex"),
  261|      6|                Regex::new(r"\bgithub_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}\b")
  262|      6|                    .expect("valid static GitHub PAT regex"),
  263|       |                // AWS access keys
  264|      6|                Regex::new(r"\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b")
  265|      6|                    .expect("valid static AWS AKIA regex"),
  266|      6|                Regex::new(r"\bASIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b")
  267|      6|                    .expect("valid static AWS ASIA regex"),
  268|       |                // Bearer / authorization tokens
  269|      6|                Regex::new(r"(?i)\bBearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9\-_\.=+/]{8,}")
  270|      6|                    .expect("valid static Bearer regex"),
  271|       |                // API keys (common prefixes)
  272|      6|                Regex::new(r"(?i)\b(?:api[_-]?key|secret[_-]?key|access[_-]?key|auth[_-]?token)\s*[:=]\s*[A-Za-z0-9\-_\.=+/]{8,}")

  274|       |            ]
  275|      6|        });

  282|  1.60k|    }

  284|       |    /// Determine if quarantine is needed based on taint score and rollback class.
  285|       |    ///
  286|       |    /// Rules:
  287|       |    /// - R0 never quarantined regardless of taint
  288|       |    /// - R3 with taint >= 70 → quarantine
  289|       |    /// - R1/R2 with taint >= 90 → quarantine
  290|      6|    pub fn should_quarantine(&self, taint_score: u8, rollback_class: RollbackClass) -> bool {
  291|      6|        match rollback_class {
  292|      3|            RollbackClass::R0 => false,
  293|      3|            RollbackClass::R3 => taint_score >= 70,
  294|      0|            RollbackClass::R1 | RollbackClass::R2 => taint_score >= 90,
  295|       |        }
  296|      6|    }

  566|       |
  567|       |/// Error type for OIDC auth failures.
  568|       |enum OidcAuthError {
  569|       |    Unauthorized(String),
  570|       |    Forbidden(String),
  571|       |}
  572|       |
  573|       |/// Validate a Bearer JWT against OIDC config.
  574|       |///
  575|       |/// Flow:
  576|       |/// 1. Decode header, select static key by `kid`.
  577|       |/// 2. If static key missing and jwks_url configured, fetch from JWKS cache.
  578|       |/// 3. Validate signature, algorithm allowlist, issuer, audience, exp, nbf.
  579|       |/// 4. Map actor_id from configured claim.
  580|       |/// 5. Map role from configured role/group claims via explicit mapping table.
  581|       |/// 6. Derive scopes via `TokenRole::default_scopes()`.
  582|       |/// 7. Enforce `required_scope_for_path()`.
  583|       |///
  584|       |/// Fail closed: any validation failure returns `OidcAuthError::Unauthorized`.
  585|       |/// Unmapped role or missing required scope returns `OidcAuthError::Forbidden`.
  586|       |/// Decode the raw JWT header segment and return true if the `alg` claim is
  587|       |/// literally `"none"`. This is a defense-in-depth check because the typed
  588|       |/// `jsonwebtoken::Algorithm` enum does not include the `none` algorithm and
  589|       |/// would otherwise reject it only as an unknown algorithm.
  590|     31|fn jwt_header_alg_is_none(token: &str) -> bool {
  591|     31|    let header_b64 = token.split('.').next().unwrap_or("");
  592|     31|    if header_b64.is_empty() {
  593|      1|        return false;
  594|     30|    }
  595|     30|    let decoded = match base64::Engine::decode(
                      ^29
  596|     30|        &base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD,
  597|     30|        header_b64,
  598|     30|    ) {
  599|     29|        Ok(bytes) => bytes,
  600|      1|        Err(_) => return false,
  601|       |    };
  602|     29|    let raw: serde_json::Value = match serde_json::from_slice(&decoded) {
                      ^28  ^28
  603|     28|        Ok(v) => v,
  604|      1|        Err(_) => return false,
  605|       |    };
  606|     28|    raw.get("alg")
  607|     28|        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
  608|     28|        .map(|s| s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("none"))
  609|     28|        .unwrap_or(false)
  610|     31|}

  620|       |    // the configured allowlist.

  644|       |            }

crates/ferrum-gateway/src/capabilities.rs:
    1|       |//! Capability governance handlers.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Routes:
    4|       |//! - `POST /v1/capabilities/mint`                    -> `mint_capability`
    5|       |//! - `POST /v1/capabilities/{capability_id}/revoke`  -> `revoke_capability`
    6|       |//!
    7|       |//! `mint_capability` mints a `CapabilityLease` through the in-memory capability
    8|       |//! service, persists it to satisfy foreign-key constraints in the `executions`
    9|       |//! and related tables, and emits a `CapabilityMinted` provenance event.
   10|       |//!
   11|       |//! `revoke_capability` first attempts an in-memory revocation. On a
   12|       |//! `NotFound` it falls back to the durable store, validates the lease
   13|       |//! status/expiry, marks the lease as revoked, and emits a
   14|       |//! `CapabilityRevoked` provenance event. Persistence is synchronous so
   15|       |//! callers observe the same state the ledger has recorded.

  718|       |            .await
  719|       |            .map_err(map_store_error)?
  720|       |            .ok_or(CapabilityError::NotFound)?;
  721|       |
  722|       |        Ok(lease)
  723|      8|    }
  724|       |
  725|       |    async fn revoke(
  726|       |        &self,
  727|       |        capability_id: CapabilityId,
  728|      8|    ) -> Result<CapabilityLease, CapabilityError> {
  729|       |        let lease = self
  730|       |            .store
  731|       |            .capabilities()
  732|       |            .get(capability_id)
  733|       |            .await
  734|       |            .map_err(map_store_error)?
  735|       |            .ok_or(CapabilityError::NotFound)?;
  736|       |
  737|       |        if matches!(lease.status, CapabilityStatus::Revoked) {
  738|       |            return Err(CapabilityError::Revoked);
  739|       |        }
  740|       |        if matches!(lease.status, CapabilityStatus::Used) {
  741|       |            return Err(CapabilityError::AlreadyUsed);
  742|       |        }
  743|       |        if lease.expires_at < Utc::now() {
  744|       |            return Err(CapabilityError::Expired);
  745|       |        }
  746|       |
  747|       |        let revoked_at = Utc::now();
  748|       |        let updated = self
  749|       |            .store
  750|       |            .capabilities()
  751|       |            .revoke_if_active(capability_id, revoked_at)
  752|       |            .await
  753|       |            .map_err(map_store_error)?;
  754|       |
  755|       |        if !updated {
  756|       |            let lease = self
  757|       |                .store
  758|       |                .capabilities()
  759|       |                .get(capability_id)
  760|       |                .await
  761|       |                .map_err(map_store_error)?
  762|       |                .ok_or(CapabilityError::NotFound)?;
  763|       |
  764|       |            if matches!(lease.status, CapabilityStatus::Used) {
  765|       |                return Err(CapabilityError::AlreadyUsed);
  766|       |            }
  767|       |            if matches!(lease.status, CapabilityStatus::Revoked) {
  768|       |                return Err(CapabilityError::Revoked);
  769|       |            }
  770|       |            if lease.expires_at < Utc::now() {
  771|       |                return Err(CapabilityError::Expired);
  772|       |            }
  773|       |            return Err(CapabilityError::NotFound);
  774|       |        }
  775|       |
  776|       |        let lease = self
  777|       |            .store
  778|       |            .capabilities()
  779|       |            .get(capability_id)
  780|       |            .await
  781|       |            .map_err(map_store_error)?
  782|       |            .ok_or(CapabilityError::NotFound)?;
  783|       |
  784|       |        Ok(lease)
  785|      8|    }
  786|       |}

 1227|      8|    async fn insert_hold(
 1228|      8|        runtime: &GatewayRuntime,
 1229|      8|        state: ferrum_proto::QuarantineHoldState,
 1230|      8|    ) -> (ferrum_proto::ProposalId, ferrum_proto::IntentId) {
 1231|      8|        let intent_id = ferrum_proto::IntentId::new();
 1232|      8|        let proposal_id = ferrum_proto::ProposalId::new();
 1233|      8|        runtime
 1234|      8|            .store
 1235|      8|            .intents()
 1236|      8|            .insert(&make_intent(intent_id))
 1237|      8|            .await
 1238|      8|            .unwrap();
 1239|      8|        runtime
 1240|      8|            .store
 1241|      8|            .proposals()
 1242|      8|            .insert(&make_proposal(proposal_id, intent_id))
 1243|      8|            .await
 1244|      8|            .unwrap();
 1245|       |
 1246|      8|        let hold = ferrum_proto::QuarantineHold {
 1247|      8|            hold_id: ferrum_proto::QuarantineHoldId::new(),
 1248|      8|            intent_id,
 1249|      8|            proposal_id,
 1250|      8|            reason: "test".to_string(),
 1251|      8|            matched_rule_ids: vec!["rule".to_string()],
 1252|      8|            policy_bundle_id: None,
 1253|      8|            state,
 1254|      8|            expires_at: chrono::Utc::now() + chrono::Duration::seconds(300),
 1255|      8|            created_at: chrono::Utc::now(),
 1256|      8|            resolved_at: None,
 1257|      8|            resolved_by: None,
 1258|      8|            resolution_reason: None,
 1259|      8|            metadata: ferrum_proto::JsonMap::new(),
 1260|      8|            owner_actor_id: None,
 1261|      8|        };
 1262|      8|        runtime
 1263|      8|            .store
 1264|      8|            .quarantine_holds()
 1265|      8|            .insert(&hold)
 1266|      8|            .await
 1267|      8|            .unwrap();
 1268|      8|        (proposal_id, intent_id)
 1269|      8|    }

    2|       |//!

    6|       |//! `Canceled`; post-side-effect states transition to `Failed`. All transitions
    7|       |//! use the store's `compare_and_set_state` so a second pass cannot double-
    8|       |//! transition an execution that has already moved to a terminal state.
    9|       |

   12|       |

   19|       |
   20|       |/// In-flight states that have not yet produced a side effect. The HA reconciler

   23|       |    ExecutionState::Proposed,
   24|       |    ExecutionState::Authorized,
   25|       |    ExecutionState::Prepared,
   26|       |    ExecutionState::AwaitingApproval,

   32|       |    ExecutionState::Running,

   85|      0|            continue;
   86|       |        };
   87|      4|        let previous_state = execution.state.clone();
   88|       |
   89|      4|        let cas_result = state
   90|      4|            .runtime
   91|      4|            .store
   92|      4|            .executions()
   93|      4|            .compare_and_set_state(
   94|      4|                execution.execution_id,
   95|      4|                &[previous_state],
   96|      4|                target_state.clone(),
   97|      4|            )
   98|      4|            .await;
   99|      4|        match cas_result {
  100|       |            Ok(true) => {
  101|      4|                match target_state {
  102|      2|                    ExecutionState::Canceled => canceled += 1,
  103|      2|                    ExecutionState::Failed => failed += 1,
  104|      0|                    _ => {}
  105|       |                }
  106|      4|                emit_ha_reconciler_provenance(state, &execution, target_state, now).await;
  107|       |            }
  108|       |            Ok(false) => {
  109|       |                // Another writer already moved the execution; skip silently.
  110|      0|                tracing::debug!(
  111|       |                    execution_id = %execution.execution_id,
  112|       |                    "ha reconciler CAS skipped execution (already transitioned)"
  113|       |                );
  114|       |            }

  116|      0|                errors += 1;
  117|      0|                tracing::error!(
  118|       |                    %error,
  119|       |                    execution_id = %execution.execution_id,
  120|       |                    "ha reconciler failed to transition stale execution"
  121|       |                );
  122|       |            }
  123|       |        }
  124|       |    }
  125|       |
  126|      6|    if canceled > 0 || failed > 0 {
                                     ^4
  127|      4|        tracing::info!(
  128|       |            canceled,
  129|       |            failed,
  130|       |            errors,
  131|       |            "ha reconciler completed pass over stale in-flight executions"
  132|       |        );
  133|      2|    }
  134|       |
  135|       |    // Update metrics counters.
  136|      6|    if canceled > 0 {
  137|      2|        state
  138|      2|            .metrics
  139|      2|            .ha_reconciler_canceled_total
  140|      2|            .fetch_add(canceled, Ordering::Relaxed);
  141|      4|    }
  142|      6|    if failed > 0 {
  143|      2|        state
  144|      2|            .metrics
  145|      2|            .ha_reconciler_failed_total
  146|      2|            .fetch_add(failed, Ordering::Relaxed);
  147|      4|    }
  148|      6|    if errors > 0 {
  149|      0|        state
  150|      0|            .metrics
  151|      0|            .ha_reconciler_errors_total
  152|      0|            .fetch_add(errors, Ordering::Relaxed);
  153|      6|    }
  154|       |
  155|      6|    (canceled, failed, errors)
  156|      6|}

  158|       |/// Background task that runs a startup scan and then periodic HA reconciler
  159|       |/// passes until the shutdown notify fires.
  160|      0|pub(crate) async fn ha_reconciler(state: Arc<AppState>, shutdown: Arc<tokio::sync::Notify>) {
  161|      0|    let interval_secs = state.server_config.ha_reconciler_interval_secs;
  162|      0|    let mut interval = tokio::time::interval(std::time::Duration::from_secs(interval_secs));
  163|      0|    interval.set_missed_tick_behavior(tokio::time::MissedTickBehavior::Delay);
  164|       |
  165|       |    loop {
  166|      0|        tokio::select! {
  167|      0|            _ = interval.tick() => {
  168|      0|                run_ha_reconciler_pass(&state).await;
  169|       |            }
  170|      0|            _ = shutdown.notified() => {
  171|      0|                tracing::info!("ha reconciler shutting down");
  172|      0|                break;
  173|       |            }
  174|       |        }
  175|       |    }

  783|       |    // Helper macro to build histogram lines for a given route/status combination
  784|       |    macro_rules! histogram_lines {
  785|       |        ($route:expr, $method:expr, $status:expr, $buckets:expr, $sum:expr, $count:expr) => {{
  786|       |            let mut lines = String::new();
  787|       |            for (i, boundary) in HISTOGRAM_BOUNDARIES.iter().enumerate() {
  788|       |                lines.push_str(&format!(
  789|       |                    "ferrumgate_request_duration_seconds{{route=\"{}\",method=\"{}\",status=\"{}\",le=\"{}\"}} {}\n",
  790|       |                    $route, $method, $status, boundary, $buckets[i]
  791|       |                ));
  792|       |            }
  793|       |            lines.push_str(&format!(
  794|       |                "ferrumgate_request_duration_seconds{{route=\"{}\",method=\"{}\",status=\"{}\",le=\"+Inf\"}} {}\n",
  795|       |                $route, $method, $status, $count
  796|       |            ));
  797|       |            lines.push_str(&format!(
  798|       |                "ferrumgate_request_duration_seconds_sum{{route=\"{}\",method=\"{}\",status=\"{}\"}} {}\n",
  799|       |                $route, $method, $status, $sum as f64 / 1e9_f64
  800|       |            ));
  801|       |            lines.push_str(&format!(
  802|       |                "ferrumgate_request_duration_seconds_count{{route=\"{}\",method=\"{}\",status=\"{}\"}} {}\n",
  803|       |                $route, $method, $status, $count
  804|       |            ));
  805|       |            lines
  806|       |        }};
  807|       |    }
  808|       |

 2676|       |    /// Prometheus metric lines in /v1/metrics output. This prevents silent observability
 2677|       |    /// gaps when new governance routes are added.

 7004|     22|    fn mint_test_jwt_with_typ(
 7005|     22|        claims: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
 7006|     22|        kid: Option<&str>,
 7007|     22|        typ: Option<&str>,
 7008|     22|    ) -> String {

 7458|      2|    fn mint_unsigned_jwt(
 7459|      2|        claims: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
 7460|      2|        _kid: Option<&str>,
 7461|      2|        typ: Option<&str>,
 7462|      2|    ) -> String {
 7463|      2|        let mut header = serde_json::Map::new();
 7464|      2|        header.insert("alg".to_string(), serde_json::json!("none"));
 7465|      2|        if let Some(t) = typ {
 7466|      2|            header.insert("typ".to_string(), serde_json::json!(t));
 7467|      2|        }
                      ^0
 7468|      2|        let header_json = serde_json::to_string(&header).unwrap();
 7469|      2|        let claims_json = serde_json::to_string(&claims).unwrap();
 7470|      2|        let header_b64 = base64::Engine::encode(
 7471|      2|            &base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD,
 7472|      2|            header_json.as_bytes(),
 7473|       |        );
 7474|      2|        let claims_b64 = base64::Engine::encode(
 7475|      2|            &base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD,
 7476|      2|            claims_json.as_bytes(),
 7477|       |        );
 7478|      2|        format!("{header_b64}.{claims_b64}.")
 7479|      2|    }

 7612|     10|        let lower = body.to_lowercase();

 7614|     10|            !lower.contains("none")
 7615|     10|                && !lower.contains("alg")

 7618|     10|                && !lower.contains("allowed")
 7619|     10|                && !lower.contains("hs256")
 7620|     10|                && !lower.contains("rs256"),
 7621|       |            "response body must not disclose algorithm or profile hints: {body}"
 7622|       |        );
 7623|     10|        let err: ApiError = serde_json::from_str(body).expect("body must be a valid ApiError");
 7624|     10|        assert_eq!(
 7625|       |            err.code,
 7626|       |            ferrum_proto::ApiErrorCode::Unauthorized,

  230|       |/// Background task that periodically reconciles stale pending quarantine holds.
  231|      1|pub(crate) async fn quarantine_timeout_reconciler(
  232|      1|    state: Arc<AppState>,
  233|      1|    shutdown: Arc<tokio::sync::Notify>,
  234|      1|) {
  235|      1|    let interval_secs = state.server_config.quarantine_reconciliation_interval_secs;
  236|      1|    let mut interval = interval(std::time::Duration::from_secs(interval_secs));
  237|      1|    interval.set_missed_tick_behavior(MissedTickBehavior::Delay);
  238|       |    loop {
  239|      1|        tokio::select! {
  240|      1|            _ = interval.tick() => {
  241|      0|                let now = Utc::now();
  242|      0|                reconcile_quarantine_timeouts_once(&state, now).await;
  243|       |            }
  244|      1|            _ = shutdown.notified() => {
  245|      1|                tracing::info!("quarantine timeout reconciler shutting down");
  246|      1|                break;
  247|       |            }
  248|       |        }
  249|       |    }

 1134|       |    #[tokio::test]
 1135|      1|    async fn approval_timeout_reconciler_shutdown_terminates_loop() {
 1136|      1|        let state = test_state().await;
 1137|      1|        tokio::time::pause();
 1138|      1|        let shutdown = Arc::new(tokio::sync::Notify::new());
 1139|      1|        let handle = tokio::spawn(approval_timeout_reconciler(state.clone(), shutdown.clone()));
 1140|       |
 1141|       |        // Yield so the spawned task enters the select! before the shutdown signal arrives.

 1145|      1|    }

   73|       |    /// Internal BFS implementation.
   74|     10|    fn bfs(&self, event_id: &str, max_hops: usize, mode: BfsMode) -> Vec<String> {
   75|     10|        let mut visited: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
   76|     10|        let mut result: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
   77|     10|        let mut queue: VecDeque<(String, usize)> = VecDeque::new();
   78|       |
   79|     10|        visited.insert(event_id.to_string());
   80|     10|        queue.push_back((event_id.to_string(), 0));
   81|       |
   82|     33|        while let Some((current, hops)) = queue.pop_front() {
                                      ^23      ^23
   83|     23|            if hops >= max_hops {
   84|      2|                continue;
   85|     21|            }
   86|       |
   87|     21|            let neighbors: Vec<String> = match mode {
   88|      6|                BfsMode::Ancestors => self.parents.get(&current).cloned().unwrap_or_default(),
   89|     12|                BfsMode::Descendants => self.children.get(&current).cloned().unwrap_or_default(),
   90|       |                BfsMode::Both => {
   91|      3|                    let mut n = self.parents.get(&current).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
   92|      3|                    if let Some(child_neighbors) = self.children.get(&current) {
   93|      3|                        n.extend(child_neighbors.iter().cloned());
   94|      3|                    }
                                  ^0
   95|      3|                    n
   96|       |                }
   97|       |            };
   98|       |
   99|     21|            for neighbor in neighbors {
                              ^16

  101|     13|                    visited.insert(neighbor.clone());
  102|     13|                    result.push(neighbor.clone());
  103|     13|                    queue.push_back((neighbor, hops + 1));
  104|     13|                }
                              ^3
  105|       |            }
  106|       |        }
  107|       |
  108|     10|        result
  109|     10|    }

  657|       |/// I7 E2E: Verify that high taint computed by TaintScoringFirewall triggers
  658|       |/// Quarantine via real StaticPdpEngine (not InjectablePdpEngine).

  664|       |///   is_external (+30) + trust_score=30<50 (+20) + privileged=true (+20) = 70
  665|       |/// - StaticPdpEngine.evaluate receives computed trust and returns Quarantine
  666|       |///
  667|       |/// This exercises the full pipeline: evaluate_proposal → build_firewall_context →
  668|       |/// TaintScoringFirewall.compute_taint_score → TrustContextSummary →
  669|       |/// StaticPdpEngine.evaluate → Decision::Quarantine
  670|       |#[tokio::test]
  671|      1|async fn test_i7_e2e_static_pdp_quarantine_on_high_taint() {
  672|      1|    let pdp = Arc::new(StaticPdpEngine); // REAL PDP, not InjectablePdpEngine
  673|      1|    let cap: Arc<dyn CapabilityService> = Arc::new(InMemoryCapabilityService::default());
  674|       |
  675|      1|    let mut registry = AdapterRegistry::default();
  676|      1|    registry.register(Arc::new(NoopRollbackAdapter::new("noop")));
  677|      1|    let rollback = Arc::new(RollbackService::new(Arc::new(registry)));
  678|       |
  679|      1|    let store = Arc::new(
  680|      1|        SqliteStore::connect("sqlite::memory:")
  681|      1|            .await
  682|      1|            .expect("connect to sqlite"),
  683|       |    );
  684|      1|    store
  685|      1|        .apply_embedded_migrations()
  686|      1|        .await
  687|      1|        .expect("apply migrations");
  688|       |

  690|       |    // This is the key difference from InjectablePdpEngine-based poisoned-context tests:
  691|       |    // the taint score is computed by TaintScoringFirewall, not injected directly.
  692|      1|    let intent_id = ferrum_proto::IntentId::new();
  693|      1|    let now = chrono::Utc::now();

  415|      2|fn compute_file_hash(path: &std::path::Path) -> String {

  417|       |    use std::io::Read;
  418|      2|    let mut file = std::fs::File::open(path).expect("open file");
  419|      2|    let mut contents = Vec::new();
  420|      2|    file.read_to_end(&mut contents).expect("read file");
  421|      2|    let mut hasher = sha2::Sha256::new();
  422|      2|    Digest::update(&mut hasher, &contents);
  423|      2|    hex::encode(hasher.finalize())

  334|       |
  335|       |    // Concurrent workers each hammer the same IP bucket until deadline

  338|      4|        let client_ip = client_ip.to_string();
  339|  11.4k|        let request_factory = move || {
                          ^4
  340|  11.4k|            axum::http::Request::builder()
  341|  11.4k|                .method(axum::http::Method::GET)

  344|  11.4k|                .header("x-real-ip", client_ip.clone())

  360|       |                // Brief yield to let other workers run
  361|  11.4k|                tokio::task::yield_now().await;
  362|       |            }
  363|      4|            (worker_id, count, results)
  364|      4|        }));
  365|       |    }
  366|       |

  372|      4|        all_statuses.extend(statuses);
  373|       |    }
  374|       |
  375|      1|    let total = all_statuses.len();

crates/ferrum-integrations-mcp/src/bin/ferrum-mcp-server.rs:
    1|       |//! # ferrum-mcp-server
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! FerrumGate MCP server binary - Phase C stdio transport + Phase D-0 REST client + Phase 6.1 HTTP transport skeleton.
    4|       |//!
    5|       |//! ## Overview
    6|       |//!
    7|       |//! This binary implements a line-based stdio JSON-RPC transport and a Streamable HTTP skeleton for FerrumGate MCP server.
    8|       |//! It reads JSON-RPC requests from stdin (stdio mode) or HTTP POST body (HTTP mode) and writes responses accordingly.
    9|       |//!
   10|       |//! ## Phase C Status
   11|       |//!
   12|       |//! Phase C implements:
   13|       |//! - Stdio line-based transport loop
   14|       |//! - Reuses `parse_request()` and `dispatch()` from `ferrum-integrations-mcp`
   15|       |//! - Handles SIGINT/SIGTERM gracefully
   16|       |//!
   17|       |//! ## Phase D-0 Status

  295|       |#[cfg(feature = "http")]
  296|       |/// Per-IP in-memory token-bucket rate limiter for the HTTP layer.
  297|       |#[derive(Debug)]
  298|       |struct IpRateLimiter {
  299|       |    rate_per_sec: f64,
  300|       |    burst: u32,
  301|       |    state: std::sync::Mutex<std::collections::HashMap<IpAddr, IpLimitState>>,
  302|       |}
  303|       |
  304|       |#[cfg(feature = "http")]
  305|       |#[derive(Debug)]
  306|       |struct IpLimitState {
  307|       |    tokens: f64,
  308|       |    last_check: std::time::Instant,
  309|       |}
  310|       |
  311|       |#[cfg(feature = "http")]
  312|       |impl IpRateLimiter {
  313|       |    fn new(rate_per_sec: f64, burst: u32) -> Self {
  314|       |        Self {
  315|       |            rate_per_sec,
  316|       |            burst,
  317|       |            state: std::sync::Mutex::new(std::collections::HashMap::new()),
  318|       |        }
  319|       |    }
  320|       |
  321|       |    fn check(&self, ip: IpAddr) -> bool {
  322|       |        self.check_at(ip, std::time::Instant::now())
  323|       |    }
  324|       |
  325|       |    fn check_at(&self, ip: IpAddr, now: std::time::Instant) -> bool {
  326|       |        let mut map = self.state.lock().unwrap();
  327|       |        let entry = map.entry(ip).or_insert(IpLimitState {
  328|       |            tokens: self.burst as f64,
  329|       |            last_check: now,
  330|       |        });
  331|       |
  332|       |        let elapsed = now.duration_since(entry.last_check).as_secs_f64();
  333|       |        entry.tokens = (entry.tokens + elapsed * self.rate_per_sec).min(self.burst as f64);
  334|       |        entry.last_check = now;
  335|       |
  336|       |        if entry.tokens >= 1.0 {
  337|       |            entry.tokens -= 1.0;
  338|       |            true
  339|       |        } else {
  340|       |            false
  341|       |        }
  342|       |    }
  343|       |
  344|       |    /// Remove entries that have been idle longer than `max_idle`.
  345|       |    fn cleanup_idle(&self, max_idle: std::time::Duration) -> usize {
  346|       |        let now = std::time::Instant::now();
  347|       |        let mut map = self.state.lock().unwrap();
  348|       |        let before = map.len();
  349|       |        map.retain(|_, state| now.duration_since(state.last_check) <= max_idle);
  350|       |        before - map.len()
  351|       |    }
  352|       |}

  374|       |#[cfg(feature = "http")]
  375|       |fn host_without_port(host: &str) -> &str {
  376|       |    if let Some(end) = host.rfind(']') {
  377|       |        // IPv6 literal including brackets.
  378|       |        &host[..=end]
  379|       |    } else if let Some(idx) = host.rfind(':') {
  380|       |        &host[..idx]
  381|       |    } else {
  382|       |        host
  383|       |    }
  384|       |}
  385|       |

  388|       |    let normalized = host_without_port(host).to_lowercase();
  389|       |    allowed.iter().any(|h| h.to_lowercase() == normalized)
  390|       |}

  413|       |#[cfg(feature = "http")]
  414|       |/// HTTP-layer security middleware: rate limiting, Host/Origin validation,
  415|       |/// and `Accept: text/event-stream` rejection.
  416|       |async fn security_middleware(
  417|       |    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
  418|       |    ConnectInfo(addr): ConnectInfo<SocketAddr>,
  419|       |    request: Request,
  420|       |    next: Next,
  421|       |) -> Response {
  422|       |    let ip = addr.ip();
  423|       |
  424|       |    if !state.ip_rate_limiter.check(ip) {
  425|       |        tracing::warn!(
  426|       |            event_type = "rate_limited",
  427|       |            remote_ip = %ip,
  428|       |            path = %request.uri().path(),
  429|       |        );
  430|       |        return (
  431|       |            StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS,
  432|       |            [(header::RETRY_AFTER, "1")],
  433|       |            serde_json::json!({ "error": "rate limit exceeded" }).to_string(),
  434|       |        )
  435|       |            .into_response();
  436|       |    }
  437|       |
  438|       |    if let Some(host) = request
  439|       |        .headers()
  440|       |        .get(header::HOST)
  441|       |        .and_then(|h| h.to_str().ok())
  442|       |    {
  443|       |        if !is_host_allowed(host, &state.allowed_hosts) {
  444|       |            tracing::warn!(
  445|       |                event_type = "host_rejected",
  446|       |                remote_ip = %ip,
  447|       |                host = %host,
  448|       |            );
  449|       |            return StatusCode::FORBIDDEN.into_response();
  450|       |        }
  451|       |    }
  452|       |
  453|       |    if let Some(origin) = request
  454|       |        .headers()
  455|       |        .get(header::ORIGIN)
  456|       |        .and_then(|o| o.to_str().ok())
  457|       |    {
  458|       |        if state.allowed_origins.is_empty()
  459|       |            || !state
  460|       |                .allowed_origins
  461|       |                .iter()
  462|       |                .any(|allowed| allowed.eq_ignore_ascii_case(origin))
  463|       |        {
  464|       |            tracing::warn!(
  465|       |                event_type = "origin_rejected",
  466|       |                remote_ip = %ip,
  467|       |                origin = %origin,
  468|       |            );
  469|       |            return StatusCode::FORBIDDEN.into_response();
  470|       |        }
  471|       |    }
  472|       |
  473|       |    // Only allow `Accept: text/event-stream` on GET /mcp. Reject it on all
  474|       |    // other paths/methods to keep SSE surface narrow.
  475|       |    if request
  476|       |        .headers()
  477|       |        .get(header::ACCEPT)
  478|       |        .and_then(|a| a.to_str().ok())
  479|       |        .is_some_and(|s| s.contains("text/event-stream"))
  480|       |    {
  481|       |        let path = request.uri().path();
  482|       |        let method = request.method();
  483|       |        if path != "/mcp" || method != Method::GET {
  484|       |            return StatusCode::NOT_ACCEPTABLE.into_response();
  485|       |        }
  486|       |    }
  487|       |
  488|       |    next.run(request).await
  489|       |}

  513|       |#[cfg(feature = "http")]
  514|       |/// Validate the `Authorization` header and return the auth fingerprint.
  515|       |///
  516|       |/// If `expected` is `Some`, the header must be a matching `Bearer <token>`.
  517|       |/// If `expected` is `None`, any bearer token is accepted (insecure mode) and
  518|       |/// an empty fingerprint is returned when no header is present.
  519|       |fn require_bearer(
  520|       |    headers: &axum::http::HeaderMap,
  521|       |    expected: Option<&str>,
  522|       |) -> Result<String, StatusCode> {
  523|       |    let auth = headers.get("Authorization").and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok());
  524|       |    match (auth, expected) {
  525|       |        (None, None) => Ok(auth_fingerprint("")),
  526|       |        (None, Some(_)) => {
  527|       |            tracing::warn!(
  528|       |                event_type = "bearer_rejected",
  529|       |                reason = "missing_or_malformed"
  530|       |            );
  531|       |            Err(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED)
  532|       |        }
  533|       |        (Some(header), expected) => {
  534|       |            const PREFIX: &str = "Bearer ";
  535|       |            if !header.starts_with(PREFIX) {
  536|       |                tracing::warn!(event_type = "bearer_rejected", reason = "missing_prefix");
  537|       |                return Err(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED);
  538|       |            }
  539|       |            let provided = &header[PREFIX.len()..];
  540|       |            if let Some(expected) = expected {
  541|       |                if !constant_time_eq(provided.as_bytes(), expected.as_bytes()) {
  542|       |                    tracing::warn!(event_type = "bearer_rejected", reason = "mismatch");
  543|       |                    return Err(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED);
  544|       |                }
  545|       |            }
  546|       |            Ok(auth_fingerprint(provided))
  547|       |        }
  548|       |    }
  549|       |}
  550|       |
  551|       |#[cfg(feature = "http")]
  552|       |/// `POST /mcp` — accept a single JSON-RPC message and return synchronous `application/json`.
  553|       |///
  554|       |/// * `initialize` creates a new session and returns `Mcp-Session-Id` on success.
  555|       |/// * All other methods require a valid `Mcp-Session-Id` header bound to the
  556|       |///   same bearer token fingerprint.
  557|       |async fn mcp_post_handler(
  558|       |    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
  559|       |    headers: axum::http::HeaderMap,
  560|       |    body: String,
  561|       |) -> Result<Response, StatusCode> {
  562|       |    let expected = state.auth_token.as_deref();
  563|       |    let fingerprint = require_bearer(&headers, expected)?;
  564|       |
  565|       |    // Parse first: invalid JSON gets a JSON-RPC parse error response without
  566|       |    // requiring a session ID.
  567|       |    let request = match parse_request(&body) {
  568|       |        Ok(req) => req,
  569|       |        Err(response) => {
  570|       |            return Ok((StatusCode::OK, axum::Json(response)).into_response());
  571|       |        }
  572|       |    };
  573|       |
  574|       |    let is_initialize = request.method == "initialize";
  575|       |
  576|       |    if is_initialize {
  577|       |        let protocol_header = HeaderName::from_static("mcp-protocol-version");
  578|       |        if let Some(version) = headers.get(&protocol_header).and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok()) {
  579|       |            if version != SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION {
  580|       |                tracing::warn!(
  581|       |                    event_type = "protocol_version_rejected",
  582|       |                    version = %version,
  583|       |                    expected = %SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
  584|       |                );
  585|       |                return Err(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
  586|       |            }
  587|       |        }
  588|       |    }
  589|       |
  590|       |    // Non-initialize requests must present a valid session ID before dispatch.
  591|       |    let session_id: Option<String> = if !is_initialize {
  592|       |        let sid = headers
  593|       |            .get("Mcp-Session-Id")
  594|       |            .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
  595|       |            .ok_or(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST)?;
  596|       |        state
  597|       |            .session_store
  598|       |            .validate_session(sid, &fingerprint)
  599|       |            .map_err(|_| StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST)?;
  600|       |        Some(sid.to_string())
  601|       |    } else {
  602|       |        None
  603|       |    };
  604|       |
  605|       |    let state_for_dispatch = Arc::clone(&state);
  606|       |    let response = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
  607|       |        dispatch_with_client(
  608|       |            request,
  609|       |            &state_for_dispatch.client,
  610|       |            &state_for_dispatch.actor.actor_id,
  611|       |            &state_for_dispatch.rate_limiter,
  612|       |        )
  613|       |    })
  614|       |    .await
  615|       |    .map_err(|_| StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR)?;
  616|       |
  617|       |    let response_json =
  618|       |        serde_json::to_string(&response).map_err(|_| StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR)?;
  619|       |
  620|       |    if is_initialize {
  621|       |        let is_success = matches!(response, JsonRpcResponse::Success(_));
  622|       |        if is_success {
  623|       |            let sid = state
  624|       |                .session_store
  625|       |                .create_session_with_fingerprint(&fingerprint)
  626|       |                .map_err(|_| StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE)?;
  627|       |            if let Err(e) = state.session_store.append_event(&sid, response_json) {
  628|       |                tracing::warn!(
  629|       |                    event_type = "replay_append_failed",
  630|       |                    error = %e,
  631|       |                    session_id = "***",
  632|       |                    "failed to append initialize response to replay buffer; returning dispatch response anyway"
  633|       |                );
  634|       |            }
  635|       |            let mut resp = (
  636|       |                StatusCode::OK,
  637|       |                [(HeaderName::from_static("mcp-session-id"), sid.as_str())],
  638|       |                axum::Json(response),
  639|       |            )
  640|       |                .into_response();
  641|       |            resp.headers_mut().insert(
  642|       |                header::CONTENT_TYPE,
  643|       |                axum::http::HeaderValue::from_static("application/json"),
  644|       |            );
  645|       |            return Ok(resp);
  646|       |        }
  647|       |    } else if let Some(sid) = session_id {
  648|       |        if let Err(e) = state.session_store.append_event(&sid, response_json) {
  649|       |            tracing::warn!(
  650|       |                event_type = "replay_append_failed",
  651|       |                error = %e,
  652|       |                session_id = "***",
  653|       |                "failed to append response to replay buffer; returning dispatch response anyway"
  654|       |            );
  655|       |        }
  656|       |    }
  657|       |
  658|       |    Ok((StatusCode::OK, axum::Json(response)).into_response())
  659|       |}
  660|       |
  661|       |#[cfg(feature = "http")]
  662|       |/// `GET /mcp` — SSE replay-only endpoint.
  663|       |///
  664|       |/// Requires bearer auth, a valid `Mcp-Session-Id`, and `Accept: text/event-stream`.
  665|       |/// Replays serialized outbound events after the optional `Last-Event-ID`.
  666|       |/// This handler never parses the request body or dispatches tool calls.
  667|       |async fn mcp_get_handler(
  668|       |    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
  669|       |    headers: axum::http::HeaderMap,
  670|       |) -> Result<Response, StatusCode> {
  671|       |    let expected = state.auth_token.as_deref();
  672|       |    let fingerprint = require_bearer(&headers, expected)?;
  673|       |
  674|       |    let accept = headers
  675|       |        .get(header::ACCEPT)
  676|       |        .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
  677|       |        .unwrap_or("");
  678|       |    if !accept.contains("text/event-stream") {
  679|       |        return Err(StatusCode::NOT_ACCEPTABLE);
  680|       |    }
  681|       |
  682|       |    let session_id = headers
  683|       |        .get("Mcp-Session-Id")
  684|       |        .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
  685|       |        .ok_or(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST)?;
  686|       |    let session = state
  687|       |        .session_store
  688|       |        .validate_session(session_id, &fingerprint)
  689|       |        .map_err(|_| StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST)?;
  690|       |
  691|       |    let last_event_id = headers.get("Last-Event-ID").and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok());
  692|       |
  693|       |    let events = session
  694|       |        .events_after(last_event_id)
  695|       |        .map_err(|_| StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST)?;
  696|       |
  697|       |    let mut body = String::new();
  698|       |    if events.is_empty() {
  699|       |        body.push_str(": heartbeat\n\n");
  700|       |    } else {
  701|       |        for event in events {
  702|       |            body.push_str(&format!("id: {}\ndata: {}\n\n", event.id, event.payload));
  703|       |        }
  704|       |    }
  705|       |
  706|       |    let mut response = (
  707|       |        StatusCode::OK,
  708|       |        [(header::CONTENT_TYPE, "text/event-stream")],
  709|       |        body,
  710|       |    )
  711|       |        .into_response();
  712|       |    response.headers_mut().insert(
  713|       |        header::CACHE_CONTROL,
  714|       |        axum::http::HeaderValue::from_static("no-store"),
  715|       |    );
  716|       |    Ok(response)
  717|       |}
  718|       |
  719|       |#[cfg(feature = "http")]
  720|       |/// `DELETE /mcp` — terminate an MCP session idempotently.
  721|       |///
  722|       |/// Requires bearer auth and a `Mcp-Session-Id` header. Returns `204 No Content`
  723|       |/// on success; unknown/expired IDs also return `204` to remain idempotent.
  724|       |async fn mcp_delete_handler(
  725|       |    State(state): State<Arc<AppState>>,
  726|       |    headers: axum::http::HeaderMap,
  727|       |) -> Result<StatusCode, StatusCode> {
  728|       |    let expected = state.auth_token.as_deref();
  729|       |    let fingerprint = require_bearer(&headers, expected)?;
  730|       |
  731|       |    let session_id = headers
  732|       |        .get("Mcp-Session-Id")
  733|       |        .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
  734|       |        .ok_or(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST)?;
  735|       |
  736|       |    // Only terminate sessions that belong to the caller; for unknown/mismatched
  737|       |    // sessions we still return 204 to avoid leaking session existence.
  738|       |    if state
  739|       |        .session_store
  740|       |        .validate_session(session_id, &fingerprint)
  741|       |        .is_ok()
  742|       |    {
  743|       |        state.session_store.terminate_session(session_id);
  744|       |    }
  745|       |    Ok(StatusCode::NO_CONTENT)
  746|       |}
  747|       |
  748|       |#[cfg(feature = "http")]
  749|       |/// Validate HTTP startup configuration and return the effective auth token.
  750|       |fn validate_http_config(
  751|       |    bind: &str,
  752|       |    auth_token: Option<String>,
  753|       |    cli: &Cli,
  754|       |) -> Result<(SocketAddr, Option<String>), String> {
  755|       |    let addr: SocketAddr = bind
  756|       |        .parse()
  757|       |        .map_err(|e| format!("Invalid bind address '{}': {}", bind, e))?;
  758|       |
  759|       |    if auth_token.is_none() && !cli.allow_insecure_no_auth {
  760|       |        return Err(
  761|       |            "HTTP transport requires a bearer token. Set FERRUM_MCP_HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN or FERRUM_GATEWAY_BEARER_TOKEN, or pass --allow-insecure-no-auth for local development only."
  762|       |                .to_string(),
  763|       |        );
  764|       |    }
  765|       |
  766|       |    if cli.allow_insecure_no_auth {
  767|       |        tracing::warn!(
  768|       |            event_type = "insecure_flag",
  769|       |            flag = "allow_insecure_no_auth",
  770|       |            "HTTP transport is running without mandatory bearer auth"
  771|       |        );
  772|       |    }
  773|       |
  774|       |    if !addr.ip().is_loopback() && !cli.allow_insecure_nonlocal_bind {
  775|       |        return Err(format!(
  776|       |            "Non-loopback bind address '{}' is not allowed. Bind to a loopback address or pass --allow-insecure-nonlocal-bind.",
  777|       |            bind
  778|       |        ));
  779|       |    }
  780|       |
  781|       |    if cli.allow_insecure_nonlocal_bind {
  782|       |        tracing::warn!(
  783|       |            event_type = "insecure_flag",
  784|       |            flag = "allow_insecure_nonlocal_bind",
  785|       |            "HTTP transport is bound to a non-loopback address"
  786|       |        );
  787|       |    }
  788|       |
  789|       |    Ok((addr, auth_token))
  790|       |}

  794|       |    std::env::var(name)
  795|       |        .ok()
  796|       |        .map(|s| {
  797|       |            s.split(',')
  798|       |                .map(|part| part.trim().to_string())
  799|       |                .filter(|part| !part.is_empty())
  800|       |                .collect()
  801|       |        })
  802|       |        .filter(|v: &Vec<String>| !v.is_empty())

  816|       |#[cfg(feature = "http")]
  817|       |/// Run the HTTP transport server.
  818|       |async fn run_http(cli: &Cli) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
  819|       |    let client = match FerrumGatewayClient::from_env() {
  820|       |        Ok(c) => c,
  821|       |        Err(e) => {
  822|       |            eprintln!(
  823|       |                "Failed to create gateway client: {}. Using default config.",
  824|       |                e
  825|       |            );
  826|       |            FerrumGatewayClient::new(&ClientConfig::default())
  827|       |                .expect("Failed to create client even with default config")
  828|       |        }
  829|       |    };
  830|       |
  831|       |    let actor = ActorIdentity::resolve(None);
  832|       |    let rate_limiter = RateLimiter::default_mcp();
  833|       |
  834|       |    // Experimental HTTP transport: read bearer token from env.
  835|       |    let auth_token = std::env::var("FERRUM_MCP_HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN")
  836|       |        .ok()
  837|       |        .or_else(|| std::env::var("FERRUM_GATEWAY_BEARER_TOKEN").ok());
  838|       |
  839|       |    let (addr, auth_token) = validate_http_config(&cli.bind, auth_token, cli)?;
  840|       |
  841|       |    let allowed_hosts = if cli.allowed_host.is_empty() {
  842|       |        let mut hosts = env_split("FERRUM_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS").unwrap_or_else(default_allowed_hosts);
  843|       |        if let Some(bind_host) = bind_host(&cli.bind) {
  844|       |            if is_loopback_bind(&cli.bind) && !hosts.contains(&bind_host) {
  845|       |                hosts.push(bind_host);
  846|       |            }
  847|       |        }
  848|       |        hosts
  849|       |    } else {
  850|       |        cli.allowed_host.clone()
  851|       |    };
  852|       |
  853|       |    let allowed_origins = if cli.allowed_origin.is_empty() {
  854|       |        env_split("FERRUM_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS").unwrap_or_default()
  855|       |    } else {
  856|       |        cli.allowed_origin.clone()
  857|       |    };
  858|       |
  859|       |    let http_rate_per_sec = cli
  860|       |        .http_rate_per_sec
  861|       |        .unwrap_or_else(|| env_or("FERRUM_MCP_HTTP_RATE_PER_SEC", 5.0));
  862|       |    let http_rate_burst = cli
  863|       |        .http_rate_burst
  864|       |        .unwrap_or_else(|| env_or("FERRUM_MCP_HTTP_RATE_BURST", 20));
  865|       |    let session_ttl = std::time::Duration::from_secs(
  866|       |        cli.mcp_session_ttl_secs
  867|       |            .unwrap_or_else(|| env_or("FERRUM_MCP_SESSION_TTL_SECS", 300_u64)),
  868|       |    );
  869|       |    let session_max_events = cli
  870|       |        .mcp_session_max_events
  871|       |        .unwrap_or_else(|| env_or("FERRUM_MCP_SESSION_MAX_EVENTS", 1000_usize));
  872|       |    let session_max_sessions = cli
  873|       |        .mcp_session_max_sessions
  874|       |        .unwrap_or_else(|| env_or("FERRUM_MCP_SESSION_MAX_SESSIONS", 1000_usize));
  875|       |    let session_max_event_bytes = cli
  876|       |        .mcp_session_max_event_bytes
  877|       |        .unwrap_or_else(|| env_or("FERRUM_MCP_SESSION_MAX_EVENT_BYTES", 1024 * 1024_usize));
  878|       |    let session_max_total_bytes = cli
  879|       |        .mcp_session_max_total_bytes
  880|       |        .unwrap_or_else(|| env_or("FERRUM_MCP_SESSION_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES", 16 * 1024 * 1024_usize));
  881|       |
  882|       |    let session_store = Arc::new(McpSessionStore::new(
  883|       |        session_ttl,
  884|       |        session_max_events,
  885|       |        session_max_sessions,
  886|       |        session_max_event_bytes,
  887|       |        session_max_total_bytes,
  888|       |    ));
  889|       |
  890|       |    let state = Arc::new(AppState {
  891|       |        client,
  892|       |        actor,
  893|       |        rate_limiter,
  894|       |        auth_token,
  895|       |        allowed_origins,
  896|       |        allowed_hosts,
  897|       |        ip_rate_limiter: Arc::new(IpRateLimiter::new(http_rate_per_sec, http_rate_burst)),
  898|       |        session_store,
  899|       |    });
  900|       |
  901|       |    let cleanup_limiter = Arc::clone(&state.ip_rate_limiter);
  902|       |    let cleanup_store = Arc::clone(&state.session_store);
  903|       |
  904|       |    let app = Router::new()
  905|       |        .route("/health", get(health_handler))
  906|       |        .route("/ready", get(ready_handler))
  907|       |        .route(
  908|       |            "/mcp",
  909|       |            post(mcp_post_handler)
  910|       |                .get(mcp_get_handler)
  911|       |                .delete(mcp_delete_handler),
  912|       |        )
  913|       |        .layer(from_fn_with_state(Arc::clone(&state), security_middleware))
  914|       |        .with_state(state);
  915|       |
  916|       |    let shutdown = Arc::new(tokio::sync::Notify::new());
  917|       |    let cleanup_shutdown = Arc::clone(&shutdown);
  918|       |    tokio::spawn(async move {
  919|       |        let mut interval = tokio::time::interval(IP_RATE_LIMITER_CLEANUP_INTERVAL);
  920|       |        interval.set_missed_tick_behavior(tokio::time::MissedTickBehavior::Delay);
  921|       |        loop {
  922|       |            tokio::select! {
  923|       |                _ = interval.tick() => {
  924|       |                    let removed = cleanup_limiter.cleanup_idle(IP_RATE_LIMITER_IDLE_TIMEOUT);
  925|       |                    tracing::debug!(event_type = "ip_rate_limiter_cleanup", removed);
  926|       |                    let expired = cleanup_store.cleanup_expired();
  927|       |                    tracing::debug!(event_type = "mcp_session_cleanup", expired);
  928|       |                }
  929|       |                _ = cleanup_shutdown.notified() => break,
  930|       |            }
  931|       |        }
  932|       |    });
  933|       |
  934|       |    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(addr).await?;
  935|       |    eprintln!("Ferrum MCP HTTP server listening on http://{}", addr);
  936|       |
  937|       |    axum::serve(
  938|       |        listener,
  939|       |        app.into_make_service_with_connect_info::<SocketAddr>(),
  940|       |    )
  941|       |    .with_graceful_shutdown(shutdown_signal(Arc::clone(&shutdown)))
  942|       |    .await?;
  943|       |    Ok(())
  944|       |}
  945|       |
  946|       |#[cfg(feature = "http")]
  947|       |async fn shutdown_signal(shutdown: Arc<tokio::sync::Notify>) {
  948|       |    let ctrl_c = async {
  949|       |        let _ = tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await;
  950|       |    };
  951|       |
  952|       |    #[cfg(unix)]
  953|       |    let terminate = async {
  954|       |        let mut sigterm = tokio::signal::unix::signal(tokio::signal::unix::SignalKind::terminate())
  955|       |            .expect("failed to install SIGTERM handler");
  956|       |        sigterm.recv().await;
  957|       |    };
  958|       |    #[cfg(not(unix))]
  959|       |    let terminate = std::future::pending::<()>();
  960|       |
  961|       |    tokio::select! {
  962|       |        _ = ctrl_c => {},
  963|       |        _ = terminate => {},
  964|       |    }
  965|       |    shutdown.notify_waiters();
  966|       |}

 1009|       |    #[test]
 1010|      1|    fn test_cli_defaults() {

 1012|      1|        assert_eq!(cli.transport, Transport::Stdio);

 1144|       |
 1145|       |    #[cfg(feature = "http")]
 1146|       |    fn test_app(
 1147|       |        auth_token: Option<String>,
 1148|       |        allowed_origins: Vec<String>,
 1149|       |        allowed_hosts: Vec<String>,
 1150|       |        session_store: Arc<McpSessionStore>,
 1151|       |    ) -> Router {
 1152|       |        // Create the blocking client on a dedicated thread to avoid
 1153|       |        // "cannot create a runtime in an async context" panic.
 1154|       |        let client =
 1155|       |            std::thread::spawn(|| FerrumGatewayClient::new(&ClientConfig::default()).unwrap())
 1156|       |                .join()
 1157|       |                .unwrap();
 1158|       |        let actor = ActorIdentity::resolve(None);
 1159|       |        let rate_limiter = RateLimiter::default_mcp();
 1160|       |        let state = Arc::new(AppState {
 1161|       |            client,
 1162|       |            actor,
 1163|       |            rate_limiter,
 1164|       |            auth_token,
 1165|       |            allowed_origins,
 1166|       |            allowed_hosts,
 1167|       |            ip_rate_limiter: Arc::new(IpRateLimiter::new(5.0, 20)),
 1168|       |            session_store,
 1169|       |        });
 1170|       |        // Leak a clone so the Arc refcount never reaches zero inside async tests,
 1171|       |        // preventing `reqwest::blocking::Client` from being dropped in an async
 1172|       |        // context (which would panic because dropping a runtime while blocking
 1173|       |        // is not allowed).
 1174|       |        let _leaked = Box::leak(Box::new(Arc::clone(&state)));
 1175|       |        Router::new()
 1176|       |            .route("/health", get(health_handler))
 1177|       |            .route("/ready", get(ready_handler))
 1178|       |            .route(
 1179|       |                "/mcp",
 1180|       |                post(mcp_post_handler)
 1181|       |                    .get(mcp_get_handler)
 1182|       |                    .delete(mcp_delete_handler),
 1183|       |            )
 1184|       |            .layer(from_fn_with_state(Arc::clone(&state), security_middleware))
 1185|       |            .with_state(state)
 1186|       |    }
 1187|       |
 1188|       |    #[cfg(feature = "http")]
 1189|       |    fn default_test_app() -> Router {
 1190|       |        let session_store = Arc::new(McpSessionStore::new(
 1191|       |            std::time::Duration::from_secs(300),
 1192|       |            1000,
 1193|       |            1000,
 1194|       |            1024 * 1024,
 1195|       |            16 * 1024 * 1024,
 1196|       |        ));
 1197|       |        test_app(
 1198|       |            Some("test-mcp-token".to_string()),
 1199|       |            vec![],
 1200|       |            default_allowed_hosts(),
 1201|       |            session_store,
 1202|       |        )
 1203|       |    }
